doc.title: Ralph Humphrey interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Amplification
summary: Humphrey says amplification is necessary for bigger venues and many kinds of music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What’s your feeling on amplification? Anything in particular?
No I think it’s necessary for certain kinds of music. Yeah. I mean I’ve played with a lot of bands and I was surrounded with speakers and a lot of that.
Yeah. It seems like society’s getting louder.

This is true, yeah. To deal just on the acoustic level is only for small acoustic groups in a cozy environment. Otherwise “turn ‘em up.” So I think it’s a necessity in a lot of cases, for bigger venues.
